articles.title: Messi celebrates his first goal since his father's death
articles.standfirst: The Argentine captain scored in the 2-2 draw against the Philadelphia Union.
articles.summary: The Argentine captain scored in the 2-2 draw against the Philadelphia Union.
articles.body:
L ionel Messi had a goal and assist as Inter Miami and the Philadelphia Union played to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday night.

Messi’s cross was headed by Luis Suarez into the path of forward Daniel Pinter for the first Inter Miami goal in the 21st minute.

Messi cut inside to his preferred left foot from 12 yards out in the 26th and curled a shot into the corner of the net for his first goal since returning to action following the death of his father.

Messi has 13 goals and nine assists in 17 MLS games this season. He has six goals and four assists in six matches in all competitions against the Union.

Indiana Vassilev scored on a volley in the first half to give the Union the lead, then 18-year-old defender Neil Pierre headed home his third goal in five games this season in the 58th minute to tie the score. Cavan Sullivan , the Union’s 16-year-old midfielder, was credited with his seventh assist of the season on Vassilev’s goal.

Union forward Milan Iloski appeared to put the Union ahead in the 62nd minute, but the goal was reviewed and waved off with Pierre offside in the buildup.

The game ended with a pair of red cards in stoppage time to Yannick Bright and Sullivan for a scuffle off the ball.

Inter Miami (11-3-6) entered the game in second place in the Eastern Conference after losing to first-place Nashville on Saturday, 4-1. Messi played 90 minutes in that loss, in which he missed a penalty, hit the post twice and assisted on Telasco Segovia’s goal . He had a game-high 11 shot attempts.

Miami had lost three straight games in all competitions entering Wednesday, having lost to a pair of Mexican clubs in the Leagues Cup. The Nashville loss ended a seven-game unbeaten run in MLS (6-0-1) dating to May 9.

Messi appeared as a sub in the Aug. 12 loss to Leon , playing 45 minutes. He missed the Aug. 8 match against Monterrey to travel home for the funeral of his father, Jorge, who died on Aug. 7.

The Union (5-10-5) are unbeaten in five games (4-0-1) since Ryan Richter was named interim coach.

Rodrigo De Paul , who like Messi was part of Argentina’s runner-up team at the World Cup , was suspended Wednesday night for yellow-card accumulation.

Inter Miami beat the Union, 6-4, on May 24 , the last game before the World Cup break for both teams. Messi didn’t have a goal, but Suarez scored a hat trick in helping Miami rally from first-half deficits for 2-0 and 3-1.

articles.title: What did Lionel Messi do? The action that was not penalized and will now be reviewed by MLS
articles.standfirst: The Argentine star scored and provided an assist in Inter Miami's 2-2 draw against the Philadelphia Union, but one scene during the match came under scrutiny
articles.summary: The Argentine star scored and provided an assist in Inter Miami's 2-2 draw against the Philadelphia Union, but one scene during the match came under scrutiny
articles.body:
The Argentine star scored and provided an assist in Inter Miami's 2-2 draw against the Philadelphia Union, but one scene during the match came under scrutiny. MLS will review the footage and Messi could receive a sanction.

Lionel Messi smiled again with a goal but had a night of mixed emotions in Philadelphia. The Argentine scored after the death of his father, Jorge Messi, and also provided an assist in Inter Miami 's 2-2 draw against the Union in a match that had tension from the start until the final minutes.

The goal that brought Messi back to celebrating was not the only thing the match left behind. The forward became the center of controversy over an incident with forward Quinn Sullivan , a Philadelphia Union player, which was not punished during the match and will now be reviewed by the MLS Disciplinary Committee.

The scene that MLS will now have to review

The episode occurred during the second half, after a specific play. Messi approached Sullivan in the middle of an argument. The footage shows the captain of Inter Miami making contact with the back of the head or neck area of the Union player before the two ended up face to face.

The referee did not show any card for that action and the match continued. However, the fact that there was no sanction during the game does not mean the incident has been put behind them: the Disciplinary Committee can review the footage and decide whether any punishment is warranted.

The situation did not end with a sending-off at that moment, but the disciplinary body has the possibility of reviewing the footage and determining whether any punishment is warranted.

A night that ended in controversy

The controversy occurred in a match that ended with a lot of tension. Inter Miami and Philadelphia drew 2-2 and, at the end, the situation ended with the send-offs of Yannick Bright, of Inter Miami, and Cavan Sullivan , of Philadelphia Union . The detail did not go unnoticed because Sullivan is also Quinn's younger brother, the same player with whom Messi had been involved minutes earlier in the controversial scene that is now under review by MLS .

In this context, the possible sanction against Messi has not yet been defined. Early reports suggest that a financial fine would be the expected scenario, although the MLS rules also contemplate a suspension.

Messi scored again, but the draw shifted the focus elsewhere

In footballing terms, Messi once again took center stage. He provided the assist for Dániel Pinté r's goal and then made it 2-1 with a left-footed strike in the 26th minute. It was his first goal since returning to action after his father's death.

Although the night ended with a question that the MLS must now answer: will there be a sanction for Messi for that action?

articles.title: MLS fines Messi for his altercation with a Philadelphia Union player
articles.standfirst: The sanction with Quinn Sullivan is for an "undisclosed" amount.
articles.summary: The sanction with Quinn Sullivan is for an "undisclosed" amount.
articles.body:
MLS announced this Friday that it fined Leo Messi for his recent altercation with Quinn Sullivan , a player for Philadelphia Union , in the latest round of the U.S. league.

"The MLS Disciplinary Committee has fined Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi an undisclosed amount for violating the League's policy regarding hands to an opponent's face/head/neck in the 101st+ minute of Miami's match against the Philadelphia Union on August 19," the league reported.

In the 2-2 draw between Inter Miami and Philadelphia, Messi confronted Sullivan and brought a hand toward his head, before the referee arrived to restore order.

Messi scored in that match the goal that made it 2-1 at the time, his first since the death of his father, Jorge Messi , to whom he dedicated the goal.

articles.title: Messi scores but can't save Inter Miami from yet another defeat, this time against Toronto FC at home
articles.standfirst: Josh Sargent and Derrick Etienne Jr. scored the goals for Toronto.
articles.summary: Josh Sargent and Derrick Etienne Jr. scored the goals for Toronto.
articles.body:
Josh Sargent and Derrick Etienne Jr. scored second-half goals three minutes apart and Toronto FC held on for a 2-1 victory over Inter Miami on Saturday night.

Neither team found the net until the rookie Sargent scored in the 59th minute to give Toronto the lead. Dániel Sallói and Etienne had assists on Sargent's fourth goal. Sallói's helper was his seventh and Etienne collected his third.

Etienne scored for the third this season — unassisted three minutes later for a two-goal lead that helped Toronto win in Miami for the first time

Lionel Messi cut it to 2-1 in the 82nd minute with his 14th goal this season and his 64th in 71 career appearances. Rodrigo De Paul had the assist.

Luka Gavran saved two shots for Toronto ( 5-7-9 ).

Dayne St. Clair finished without a save for Inter Miami ( 11-4-6 ), which falls to 0-2-2 in August.

Toronto is 2-0-2 in its last four matches and 2-1-4 since July 1.

Inter Miami posted a 4-2 victory in Toronto back in May and leads the all-time series 9-3-2.

articles.title: Inter Miami's crisis won't stop Messi from “giving Cristiano Ronaldo a run for his money” in their race for the 1,000th goal
articles.standfirst: Lionel Messi is trailing Cristiano Ronaldo in the historic scoring chase, but his remarkable efficiency means the Argentine cannot be ruled out despite Inter Miami's struggles
articles.summary: Lionel Messi is trailing Cristiano Ronaldo in the historic scoring chase, but his remarkable efficiency means the Argentine cannot be ruled out despite Inter Miami's struggles
articles.body:
Lionel Messi 's pursuit of 1,000 career goals has taken another twist, with the Inter Miami superstar continuing to close in on Cristiano Ronaldo despite his club's increasingly difficult run of form.

Inter Miami 's problems have become impossible to ignore. The Herons suffered a 2-1 home defeat to Toronto FC on Saturday, extending their winless run to five matches and leaving them with four defeats in their last five games.

Messi scored again, but his effort was not enough to prevent another setback. For Messi , however, the individual milestone remains within sight.

The Argentine has already surpassed the 900-goal mark for his senior career, and his latest goal against Toronto took his tally to 923. Cristiano Ronaldo, meanwhile, is considerably closer to the landmark, having reached 978 after scoring against Al-Riyadh on August 21. That leaves the Portuguese forward needing only 22 more goals to reach 1,000.

That gap makes Ronaldo the clear favorite to get there first, but Messi's scoring rate means the race is far from irrelevant.

The two greatest forwards of their generation have spent much of their careers being compared, from their battles for the Ballon d'Or to their extraordinary scoring records. Now, at the respective ends of their careers, another statistical competition has emerged.

Messi has more ground to make up, but the numbers remain remarkable

Ronaldo's advantage is largely the result of longevity. The 41-year-old has played more games than Messi and has continued to score at an extraordinary rate well into his forties.

The Al Nassr forward entered the new season needing only a relatively modest number of goals to reach four figures. He has also shown repeatedly that age has not stopped him from producing prolific numbers, having scored 50, 35 and 30 league goals across his previous three Saudi Pro League campaigns.

Messi's task is substantially harder. At 39, he needs roughly 77 more goals from his current tally to reach 1,000. Yet there is an argument that the Argentine's efficiency gives him a genuine chance to remain in the conversation.

A recent comparison by AS noted that Messi has historically scored more frequently in terms of minutes per goal than Ronaldo , despite the Portuguese star having accumulated more goals overall. Messi has also rediscovered his club scoring touch since joining Inter Miami, scoring 90 goals in 104 appearances for the Herons according to the outlet's figures.

That productivity is particularly important because Messi does not need to match Ronaldo goal for goal to make the chase interesting. He simply needs to maintain a high enough scoring rate and continue playing for several more seasons.

The Inter Miami situation could make that more difficult. The club's recent slump has put greater pressure on Messi to produce, while the team is also dealing with a demanding schedule. The Herons have struggled to turn his individual contributions into results, even as he continues to find the net.

Messi's personal circumstances have also made his recent performances more remarkable. His father, Jorge Messi , died on August 8 at the age of 68, yet Messi returned to action and scored his first goal since the loss against the Philadelphia Union , dedicating the moment to his father.

The latest Toronto goal showed the same pattern: Messi continues to deliver individually even when Miami cannot find a way to win.

Ronaldo therefore remains firmly in control of the 1,000-goal race. With fewer than two dozen goals separating him from the landmark, he could potentially reach it during the 2026-27 campaign.

Messi's route is much longer, and whether he gets there may ultimately depend on how long he chooses to continue playing. But the Argentine has already demonstrated that counting him out is dangerous.

Inter Miami may be in crisis, but Messi's scoring production has not disappeared. If he maintains that level for the next few years, he could still “give Cristiano Ronaldo a run for his money” in one of the most remarkable individual races football has ever seen.

articles.title: Inter Miami must make major decision that Lionel Messi won’t like, but they can no longer wait
articles.standfirst: It’s become clear what Miami’s biggest problem is, and the club must soon take action before their season crumbles.
articles.summary: It’s become clear what Miami’s biggest problem is, and the club must soon take action before their season crumbles.
articles.body:
From a small picture perspective, things aren’t actually that bad for Inter Miami . They sit in second place in the Eastern Conference, in what would be a prime position during the MLS Playoffs . From a big picture perspective, the club is in absolute shambles.

Inter Miami haven’t won a game since August 5 . Since then, they’ve played five games and lost four of them . They’ve given up 13 goals in those games. And what’s worse is that Lionel Messi only missed one of those games; even with their superstar captain back for the past four games, the team can’t stop their slide.

Naturally, plenty of finger-pointing has begun. The defensive back line has never been a strength of the team, but it seems almost impossible to defend so poorly , especially with defensive midfielder Casemiro being brought into the squad. That has many fans pointing the finger at Guillermo Hoyos , the manager who replaced Javier Mascherano when the latter resigned in April.

Guillermo Hoyos doesn't appear to be a manager who can turn things around for Inter Miami

Hoyos has had a long but not overly successful managerial career , unable to stay with a club for very long and never managing any elite teams. But Hoyos has what many other managers don’t: A personal relationship with Messi that spans across two decades . Unfortunately, that isn’t enough to win games .

The Athletic’s Felipe Cardenas recently delved into why Hoyos was “ an unserious hire blessed by Messi ” who was simply under qualified. And if Miami want to turn things around, they likely have to remove him from the position.

“Trust in God” was one of Hoyos’ solutions to Miami’s current run of results. He also blamed the congested football calendar and heat and humidity of South Florida as reasons for his team’s below-average play. Those are valid points, but the calendar and weather are two factors that Hoyos cannot control or change. He can improve Miami’s tactics or find new ways to motivate a team that includes World Cup winners and experienced internationals. But therein lies the problem. ​ ​Hoyos’ coaching resumé wouldn’t get him through the door at any of the 10 biggest clubs in the world. It wouldn’t get him a job in MLS other than the one he has in Miami… Miami’s laundry list of tactical problems appears too much for Hoyos and his staff to solve.

Miami have long done what they believe would appease Messi and keep him happy . So far, that has worked out swimmingly. But this is a situation that may not be able to be corrected by Hoyos, and the club must take action sooner than later.

articles.title: Who is Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez, Lionel Messi's new manager at Inter Miami?
articles.standfirst: Inter Miami are set to appoint a fourth-consecutive Argentinian manager amidst a brutal five-game stretch.
articles.summary: Inter Miami are set to appoint a fourth-consecutive Argentinian manager amidst a brutal five-game stretch.
articles.body:
It was bound to happen after a truly brutal five-game stretch: Inter Miami are making a switch at manager . Guillermo Hoyos , who took over once Javier Mascherano resigned in April, had looked out of his depth as of late.

Coming in to replace Hoyos will reportedly be Cristian Gonzalez , who's known more as "Kily" Gonzalez . Miami are hoping Gonzalez can turn things around right before the MLS Playoffs begin. Superstar team captain Lionel Messi has played extremely well since returning from mourning his father's death in Argentina, but the rest of the team has struggled mightily .

Kily Gonzalez has known Lionel Messi for a long time

Just as with the last three managers, all born in Argentina, Gonzalez has a personal link to Messi . Both Gonzalez and Messi were born in Rosario , and they actually spent time together on the Argentina national team for two qualifying matches ahead of the 2006 FIFA World Cup .

Back in 2022, right after winning the 2022 FIFA World Cup , Gonzalez greeted Messi and Angel Di Maria when both arrived to Rosario . They also took part together in Maxi Rodriguez 's farewell match in the city.

Gonzalez doesn't necessarily have the strongest managerial resume. He spent under two years with both Rosario Central and Union Santa Fe . His most recent sting, with Platense , lasted just 132 days.

Platense : 2 wins, 5 draws, 7 losses

Union Santa Fe : 25 wins, 25 draws, 27 losses

Rosario Central : 25 wins, 14 draws, 29 losses

Miami is hoping he brings something different to Inter.

articles.title: Can Antoine Griezmann lead Orlando City on a championship run?
articles.standfirst: The World Cup champion has started all six regular-season matches, while contributing three goals and two assists
articles.summary: The World Cup champion has started all six regular-season matches, while contributing three goals and two assists
articles.body:
The question sounded ambitious when Antoine Griezmann first arrived in Major League Soccer. Could a 35-year-old World Cup winner, fresh off a decorated career in Europe, really transform Orlando City SC from a team sitting outside the playoff picture into a legitimate MLS Cup contender?

Six matches into his MLS c areer, that question no longer feels far-fetched. In fact, after another match-winning performance that earned him MLS Player of the Matchday honors , the better question might be this: How far can Griezmann take Orlando ?

A transformational arrival

When Orlando City signed Griezmann from Atlético Madrid , the move immediately became one of the biggest stories in MLS. The French forward arrived with a résumé that few players in league history could match. A FIFA World Cup champion with France, a UEFA Champions League veteran , and one of the most accomplished attackers of his generation, Griezmann brought star power and elite experience to Central Florida.

Since joining Orlando, Griezmann has started all six regular-season matches, playing every minute available while contributing three goals and two assists. The team has gone 3-2-1 during that stretch, with all six matches coming against teams currently positioned in the MLS Cup Playoffs race.

Before Griezmann's arrival, Orlando had accumulated just 14 points and sat 12th in the Eastern Conference , outside the playoff picture. Following the club's recent victory over Real Salt Lake , the Lions climbed into ninth place and currently occupy a playoff spot.

The match that showed his value

Griezmann's performance against Real Salt Lake may have been the clearest indication yet of what he can mean to Orlando's championship aspirations. With the Lions trailing in the second half, the Frenchman delivered exactly the type of moment elite players are expected to produce.

In the 53rd minute, he pounced on a loose ball inside the six-yard box and calmly finished to level the match. With nine minutes remaining, Griezmann collected the ball, weaved through multiple defenders, and scored the game-winning goal that sent Inter&Co Stadium into celebration.

The brace was his first in MLS and earned him Player of the Matchday recognition. It was also the kind of performance championship contenders rely on from their biggest stars. MLS history is filled with examples of teams that found another level after adding a proven international star.

What separates Griezmann from many high-profile imports is that he has not arrived merely as a recognizable name. He has immediately become one of Orlando's most influential players. His movement creates opportunities for teammates. His vision unlocks defenses. His ability to score and create chances forces opponents to adjust their game plans. Just as important, Antoine brings experience from football's biggest stages.
